0.long_answer: The parasite in question is Toxoplasma gondii. This parasite is commonly associated with chorioretinitis, especially in individuals with compromised immune systems. When acquired congenitally, Toxoplasma gondii infection can lead to the classic triad of symptoms in newborns, which includes chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and cerebral calcifications. The congenital form of the disease, known as congenital toxoplasmosis, results from the transmission of the parasite from an infected mother to her fetus during pregnancy. In addition to these primary manifestations, congenital toxoplasmosis can also cause other complications such as seizures, developmental delays, and sensorineural hearing loss.
